body.p: Rewrite the pending claims and add new claims as follows:

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) An apparatus for measuring magnetic fields from a subject's organ, comprising:a plurality of unshielded magnetometers in a three-dimensional arrangement,
wherein:
a respective pair of magnetometers, in the plurality of magnetometers, has a respective known separation;
each magnetometer in the plurality of magnetometers is configured to simultaneously detect a biomagnetic field from at least a portion of the subject's organ and a background magnetic field and output a signal indicative of the detected biomagnetic field and the background magnetic field;
the plurality of magnetometers are spatially distributed such that in Fourier space the plurality of magnetometers have a wavevector coverage to recover information from both the biomagnetic field from the subject's organ and the background magnetic field;
and the apparatus is configured to operate without magnetic shielding.
2. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein each magnetometer in the plurality of magnetometers is responsive to a total magnetic field in proximity to the respective magnetometer.
3. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the respective known separation has a respective fixed length.
4. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein:
the plurality of magnetometers includes a first magnetometer having a variable position; and
a respective pair of magnetometers, in the plurality of magnetometers, has a respective known separation that varies during device operation and determined by tracking a position of the first magnetometer.
5. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the background magnetic field includes a uniform magnetic field.
6. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the plurality of magnetometers has an average spacing that satisfies a constraint in the Fourier space, such that the average spacing provides a wavevector coverage to recover information from both the biomagnetic field from the subject's organ and the background magnetic field.
7. (Canceled)
8. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein:
the plurality of magnetometers comprises an array of magnetometers arranged in a stack of planes, wherein:
adjacent magnetometers in a respective plane of the stack of planes are separated by a first predefined spacing along a length of the array and separated by a second predefined spacing along a width of the array; and
magnetometers in adjacent planes of the stack of planes are separated by a third predefined spacing along a thickness direction of the array.
9. (Original) The apparatus of claim 8, wherein:
a first magnetometer in a first plane of the stack of planes is aligned with a second magnetometer in a second plane of the stack of planes along the length and the width of the array.
10. (Original) The apparatus of claim 8, wherein:the array of magnetometers includes a first subset of magnetometers positioned in a first plane of the stack of planes and a second subset of magnetometers positioned in a second plane of the stack of planes; and
the first subset of magnetometers are aligned with the second subset of magnetometers along the length and the width of the array.
11. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 8, wherein each of the magnetometers in the array comprises:an optically pumped magnetometer; or a diamond [[NV]] nitrogen vacancy (NV) center magnetometer; or a fluxgate sensor.
12. (Original) The apparatus of claim 8, wherein the apparatus is operable at room temperature.
13. (Original) The apparatus of claim 8, wherein each magnetometer in the array of magnetometers has a sensitivity better than 100 .SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.260.22
14. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein each magnetometer of the plurality of unshielded magnetometers has a dynamic range of around 50 microTeslas.
15. and the magnetometer system is configured to operate without magnetic shielding;one or more processors; and

16. (Currently Amended) The magnetometer system of claim 15, wherein the stored instructions include signal processing instructions to separate the background field from the biomagnetic field signals.
17. (Original) The magnetometer system of claim 15, wherein the plurality of magnetometers are positioned within a housing.
18. (Original) The magnetometer system of claim 15, further comprising:a positioning arm for supporting the plurality of unshielded magnetometers.
19. (Original) The magnetometer system of claim 18, wherein the positioning arm is mounted on a base that includes one or more wheels.
20. (Original) The magnetometer system of claim 18, wherein the positioning arm is mounted on a patient support platform.
21. (Currently Amended) The magnetometer system of claim 15, wherein each of the plurality of unshielded magnetometers comprises:an optically pumped magnetometer; or a diamond [[NV]] nitrogen vacancy (NV) center magnetometer; or a fluxgate sensor.
